PD DATA STATISTICAL SUMMARY – 2010 issue 
Comparison to Similar Machines 
Data collected from the same machine operating under similar 
parameters using the same test setup are directly comparable and the 
most useful. It is also possible to roughly compare the results of one 
machine to those of similar machines. Due to the influence of the test 
frequency on the results, the test setup (sensors and test instrument) 
must be the same for all comparisons. Based on statistical analysis, the 
type of machine does not appear to have a great impact to PD levels 
and though insulation types have different types of failure mechanisms, 
in these gross comparisons there does not appear to be much difference 
in the overall levels of PD activity. Load and temperature can also greatly influence test results, but these 
are dependent upon the type and condition of the insulation system, and thus, cannot be used in these gross 
comparisons. The remaining operating variables – voltage and gas coolant – must be similar to compare 
results. 
Tables 1-6 are statistical summaries of the Qm values based on the 2009 Iris database that contains over 
226,750 test results. Data are separated by sensor, gas coolant, and voltage class. All of the data was 
acquired using an Iris test instrument, a PDA-IV, TGA or Guard. Each table shows the average, maximum, 
and the 25th, 50th, 75th, 90th, and 95th percentile ranks. The 25th percentile is the Qm magnitude for which 
25% of the test results are below, similarly for 50%, 75%, 90% and 95%. Normally, there is concern for a 
winding if the Qm in a machine is higher than the 90th percentile and increasing.
